edits.html: How NBME framed it A murmur new on day 3 after a normal birth examination pulls toward a ventricular septal defect or patent ductus arteriosus; its soft grade and spread to the axilla mark peripheral pulmonary stenosis. The options were the five common acyanotic lesions, so the key was the umbrella term, pulmonary stenosis.

How NBME framed it No organism or granuloma was named; the clue was a maternal uncle who died of fungal pneumonia, which points to X-linked disease. Four of the five options were steps in leukocyte function, and the key named the killing defect as impaired microbicidal activity.
